intro: On the eastern shore of the Dardanelles, in Çanakkale province, lie the remains of Lampsacus, an ancient city of the 7th century BC – 4th century AD. It was famous for two things: its mint and the cult of Priapus.
history: Phocaean colonists founded the city in the 7th century BC. Its strategic position by the straits brought trade, and trade brought wealth. Under Persia and Rome, Lampsacus remained a cultural centre — and its name lives on today in the modern town of Lapseki.
structure-1: You are now in front of the Altar of Zeus. Here, sacrifices and offerings were made in his honour. Pause for a moment at this sacred spot.
structure-2: This is the Sanctuary of Priapus, a sacred precinct dedicated to the god of fertility. Take a moment in the place where the city honoured him.
structure-5: And here is the Coin Mint, the official building where the city struck its coinage. Listen, and you might almost hear the ring of metal being struck.
highlights: As you wander, don't miss the Ancient Harbour and the City Walls.
facts: Did you know? Lampsacus had one of the richest mints in the ancient world, and its patron god, Priapus, was the deity of gardens. The Persian king Artaxerxes granted the city to the exiled Athenian Themistocles to cover his wine. The philosopher Anaxagoras died here, and the city honoured his memory with an annual school holiday for its children. And as the centre of the cult of Priapus, its name recurs again and again in ancient literature.
outro: This brings our journey through Lampsacus to an end. Before you go, a small request: please leave the stones untouched, keep to the marked paths and carry water with you. These stones have waited for centuries; let them keep waiting for those who come after you. Enjoy your visit.
